conditions: APInex's official APInexGate page describes its MIT-licensed storefront as a reseller platform using one APInex upstream key, customer gateway keys, retail markup and subscriptions; this establishes a candidate program description, not a verified API service agreement.

Obtain and review complete current APInex Terms and applicable upstream account/plan terms before any use; the current official legal page identifies the Terms but its substantive clauses/date were not readable in this public refresh.
The reseller landing page and public model catalog claim 53 models, while the reseller guide body says 36+; neither number establishes which models an APInex upstream account can use.
Do not treat APInexGate's MIT software license as permission under APInex upstream service terms, upstream model-provider terms, or model licenses.

For each model, record APInex as gateway/account provider, the actual underlying serving provider, the publisher and exact model license separately; public IDs, wholesale price examples and free/* labels do not establish rights or a route entitlement.
Confirm live upstream model supply, endpoint/account capability, quota, current quote and availability from authorized public or account-scoped material before any future rule consideration.
If the model requires payment, do not rely on projections or sample markups as supplier quote or Vrooli customer price; all trust, price and activation remain separate human decisions.

Because current service terms could not be read and model/operator rights remain unresolved, this is a denied conditional candidate only, not an approved supplier rule or serving entitlement.

research.model_reason: APInexGate docs describe proxying one APInex upstream key but do not establish actual serving providers, upstream publisher/model rights, current entitlement or per-model route availability. Public reseller materials conflict on their catalog count (53 versus 36+), and no substantive API Terms or downstream grant was readable.
